device.name: Isaac Lab Flamingo velocity flat constraint task

facts.text: Isaac-Velocity-Flat-Flamingo-v1-ppo-constraint is registered with entry point lab.flamingo.isaaclab.isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedConstraintRLEnv and the FlamingoFlatEnvCfg configuration
The environment class is a Gymnasium Env for a vectorized manager-based workflow: ManagerBasedConstraintRLEnv(ManagerBasedEnv, gym.Env)

The default action terms are six joint-position targets for the left/right hip, shoulder and leg joints with scale 2.0 and two wheel-velocity targets for the left/right wheel joints with scale 20.0, so the action has eight values
The action space is Box(low=-inf, high=inf) with shape (action_dim,) and the observation space is a Dict of Box(low=-inf, high=inf) groups, both batched over num_envs
The flat velocity config defaults to 4096 parallel environments
The flat velocity config sets decimation 4 and sim.dt 0.005 s, so one environment step advances 20 ms of simulated time
The Flamingo velocity flat task sets episode_length_s to 20.0 s
max_episode_length is ceil(episode_length_s / step_dt), 1000 steps for 20 s at 20 ms per step
The time_out constraint truncates the episode when episode_length_buf reaches max_episode_length
The base_contact constraint terminates on a contact force above 1.0 on base_link, hip, shoulder or leg bodies
The stack_policy observation group concatenates joint_pos, joint_vel, base_ang_vel, base_euler and actions terms in that order

step processes the action, runs the simulation for cfg.decimation steps, computes the constraint and reward buffers, resets terminated environments, computes observations and returns observations, rewards, reset_delta, reset_time_outs and extras
The README targets Isaac Sim 4.5, Isaac Lab 2.0.0, Python 3.10 and Linux
The package is installed with pip install -e . from the repository root
The USD assets are not uploaded by git and must be unzipped manually under the assets folder
The training script creates the task with gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg, render_mode=...)
The training script seeds the environment with env.seed(agent_cfg.seed)

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) and cap.world.seed.v1 set the seed of the next reset (scripts/co_rl/train.py:162 seeds the upstream environment the same way). The fake's reduced state is deterministic; its seed does not change the fixed initial observation. The upstream Isaac Sim environment was not run here, so its own determinism is not claimed.

gaps: the fake is an interface stand-in: it models no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuator, sensor or noise model; the upstream task runs Isaac Sim 4.5 and Isaac Lab 2.0.0 (README.md:3-5), which this package does not install or run, and no simulator run is claimed

the fake serves one environment with the 8-value action of the default FlamingoFlatEnvCfg and a 28-value stack_policy observation, while the upstream spaces are batched over 4096 environments and its observation_space is a Dict of four groups (stack_policy, none_stack_policy, stack_critic, none_stack_critic); the other groups are not represented

the fake's 28-value observation follows the stack_policy term order (joint position 6, joint velocity 8, base angular velocity 3, base Euler 3, last action 8); every value except the last action is a fixed placeholder, and no robot pose, command, contact, height scan or reward is simulated
the fake truncates at 1000 steps (20.0 s at 20 ms per step) and never terminates on contact: the base_contact constraint (threshold 1.0) and the terrain constraint are not modelled
no snapshot or restore: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state and the fake offers none
only the fake backend is declared; opening the registered task through gymnasium.make needs Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab and a task cfg, and was not run

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
